minutes.headline: ZBA granted a special permit to separate the Meisners' merged Jocelyn Street lots, on a trust condition
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard a petition for a special permit for dimensional variation for 51 Jocelyn Street, a lot that merged with the applicants' house lot at 49 after a 2006 refinance. Members debated whether the board had power to undo a merger and whether to ask town counsel. A motion to grant, on condition that 49 Jocelyn Street go back into a trust, was seconded and the chair indicated it carried despite one abstention.

public_comment.topic: Applicant David Meisner said the lot was taken out of trust by mistake at a closing and asked for a favorable decision.
Spoke in favor; the town sold the lot in 2003, and a new house would add tax revenue and new growth.
Applicant Diane Meisner explained there were two separate mortgages and that financial hardship, possibly bankruptcy, would follow if the lot could not be sold.

votes.motion: Allow separation of the two lots, as amended and restated to grant the special permit on condition that 49 Jocelyn Street be put back into a trust.
votes.outcome: passed, with one abstention (count not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicants bought the lot from the town in 2003.
A speaker said the lot pays a small annual tax and a house would add revenue.
The building official said that if relief is granted, a privilege fee roughly equal to a betterment would apply; who pays was unsettled.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit allowing two merged lots at 49 and 51 Jocelyn Street to be separated, on condition that 49 Jocelyn Street be put back into a trust.
The chair indicated the motion carried with one abstention; the count was not stated in the minutes.
Members debated whether the board has power to undo a merger and whether to ask town counsel, and the discussion ended without a resolution on that question.
The chair read the findings and conditions, including compliance with all licenses and regulations, and advised on the appeal period and recording at the registry of deeds.
The building official said that if relief is granted, a sewer privilege fee roughly equal to a betterment would apply; who pays it was left unsettled.

why_it_matters: The decision lets a lot the town sold in 2003 be built on separately, which would add a taxable house to the tax rolls and bring a sewer connection charge.
The board granted the permit while its power to undo a merger was still debated and no advice from town counsel was recorded, so the appeal period matters for whether the decision stands.
